A real DNSSEC delegation chain, captured from the live DNS.

Collected 2026-08-16 (unix 1786866288) over UDP/53 from 8.8.8.8 with the DO
bit set, for the apex `cloudflare.com.`:

  cloudflare-com.der          the chain as this design encodes it — DER
                              `SEQUENCE OF SEQUENCE { IA5String, OCTET STRING }`,
                              apex link first, root link last:
                                link 0  cloudflare.com.  DS + RRSIG      (175 B)
                                link 1  com.             DNSKEY + RRSIG
                                                       + DS + RRSIG      (609 B)
                                link 2  .                DNSKEY + RRSIG (1111 B)
                              1947 bytes of DER in total.
  cloudflare-com-dnskey.bin   the wire DNSKEY rdata of cloudflare.com's KSK
                              (flags 257, protocol 3, algorithm 13, key tag
                              2371) — the key the apex DS covers, which a
                              monitor derives from a certificate's SPKI and
                              never asks DNS for.

Nothing in this repository authored any of these bytes. They exercise the
parts of `synch_net::chain` a synthetic zone cannot: RSASHA256 (algorithm 8)
at the root, ECDSAP256SHA256 (algorithm 13) at `com.` and below, a real
multi-level DS ladder, real RRSIG canonical-form serialization, and the ICANN
root trust anchor hickory ships (KSK-2017, tag 20326).

These RRSIGs expire weeks after capture, which is exactly the point: the
validator never looks at a clock, so this fixture keeps verifying for as long
as the keys themselves stand. It will finally stop verifying when `com.` or
the root rotates the *keys* — at which point the fixture is regenerated with
the script recorded in docs/REKOR-ZONE-KEY.md §9.
